IIII.}}</noinclude>Iacob: Whereas in deede that Patriarch adoring there before the Temple was appointed, or the Lavv giuen, made nothing for their Schi{{ls}}me: Which was begone by Mana{{ls}}{{ls}}es a fugitiue Prie{{ls}}t, onely to hold his vnlavvful wife thereby, and to obtaine Superioritie, in Schi{{ls}}me: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io{{ls}}eph. li. antiq. 11. c. 8''.}}vvhich he could not doe in the vnitie of his brethren: long after the Temple of Hieru{{ls}}alem, from vvhich the reuolt was made. Therfore Chri{{ls}}t giueth {{ls}}entence for the Ievves and the Temple of Hieru{{ls}}alem, affirming that they had a good ground thereof, but the Samaritanes none at al. Io{{ls}}ephus al{{ls}}o recordeth how the Samaritanes demaunded of Alexander the Great, the like priuileges and immunities as he had graunted to the high Prie{{ls}}t and Temple of Hieru{{ls}}alem, pretending their Temple to be as great and as worthy, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The true Temple preuaileth.}}and them {{ls}}elues to be Ievves as the other, and to vvor{{ls}}hip the {{ls}}ame God. but their Schi{{ls}}matical hypocri{{ls}}ie was ea{{ls}}ely {{ls}}pied and dimi{{ls}}{{ls}}ed vvith nothing. An other time the Ievves and Samaritanes (as the {{ls}}ame writer te{{ls}}tifieth) {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io{{ls}}eph. li. 13. antiq. c. 6''.}}made a great {{ls}}turre in Alexandria about the truth and antiquitie of the Schi{{ls}}matical temple and {{ls}}eruice in Garîzim and the other true Temple of Salomon: in {{ls}}o much that the matter was put to arbitrement by Ptolomæus the kings commaundement, onely to trie whether of the two was fir{{ls}}t. And the Schi{{ls}}matikes (as their cu{{ls}}tome is) ''per {{ls}}altum'' can make their Church or {{ls}}eruice as old as they li{{ls}}t, referring it to the Patriarches, as our Schi{{ls}}matikes do now to Chri{{ls}}t and the Apo{{ls}}tles. But when the trial was made, onely they of Hieru{{ls}}alem did inuincibly proue by continual {{ls}}ucce{{ls}}{{ls}}ion of their Prie{{ls}}ts, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The true Temple is proued by continual {{ls}}ucce{{ls}}{{ls}}ion.}}and by the iu{{ls}}t note of the time when the Schi{{ls}}matikes went out from them, that theirs was the lavvful, and the other the fal{{ls}}e temple and fal{{ls}}e adoration. and {{ls}}o it was iudged, and the Samaritanes put to {{ls}}ilence. Afterward the {{ls}}aid Schi{{ls}}matikes (which is lightly the end of al Schi{{ls}}mes) reuolted quite from the Iewes religion, and dedicated their temple in Garizim to Iupiter Olympius, as Caluins {{ls}}upper and his bread and wine is like at length to come to the {{ls}}acrifice of Ceres and Bacchus.

Our Sauiour foretelleth her that the end & cea{{ls}}ing of their {{ls}}acrifice & adoration in both the Temples {{ls}}hould {{ls}}hortly be, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Chri{{ls}}tian adoration throughout al nations in euery place, in {{ls}}pirit & veritie: that is, in the Sacraments and {{ls}}eruice of the new law, ful of {{ls}}pirit & grace: in the veritie of things before prefigured, {{ls}}pecially the true {{ls}}acrifice of Chri{{ls}}ts body and bloud.}}and euen then vvas begone to be fulfilled: in{{ls}}tructing her in three things concerning that point. fir{{ls}}t, that the true Sacrifice {{ls}}hould be tied no more to that one place or nation, but that true adoration {{ls}}hould be through out al Nations according to the Prophecie of Malachie. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 1, 11''.}}Secondly, that the gro{{ls}}{{ls}}e and carnal adoration by the fle{{ls}}h and bloud of bea{{ls}}tes and other external terrene creatures, not hauing in them grace, {{ls}}pirit, and life, {{ls}}hould be taken away, & an other {{ls}}acrifice {{ls}}ucceede, which {{ls}}hould be in it {{ls}}elf inui{{ls}}ible, cele{{ls}}tial, diuine, ful of life, Spirit, and grace, and thirdly, that this adoration and {{ls}}acrifice {{ls}}hould be the veritie it {{ls}}elf, whereof al the former {{ls}}acrifices and ho{{ls}}tes were but {{ls}}hadowes and figures, and he calleth that here {{ls}}pirit and truth, which in the fir{{ls}}t Chapter is called grace and truth. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 17.''}}Al vvhich is no more but a prophecie and de{{ls}}cription of the Sacrifice of the faithful Gentils in the body and bloud of Chri{{ls}}t: not that it is not by external meanes giuen to vs (for othervvi{{ls}}e vve being men con{{ls}}i{{ls}}ting of fle{{ls}}h and bloud could not be capable thereof) but that it is {{ls}}pirit and life in it {{ls}}elf, being the fle{{ls}}h of the {{sc|Word}} of God. And if a man enlarge the vvord of Adoration, (vvhich here as is {{ls}}aid, {{ls}}ignifieth properly the wor{{ls}}hip of God by {{ls}}acrifice) to al the Sacraments of the new Law, they al likewi{{ls}}e be {{ls}}pirit and grace, the Holy Gho{{ls}}t working inui{{ls}}ibly and internally vpon our {{ls}}oules by euery one of them. Wherevpon our Bapti{{ls}}me, is water & the Holy Gho{{ls}}t: our Penance, the word of ab{{ls}}olution and the Holy Gho{{ls}}t: our Confirmation, oile & the Holy Gho{{ls}}t by impo{{ls}}ition of handes: finally, al the adoration of the Catholike Church, is properly {{ls}}piritual, though certaine external creatures for our natures, {{ls}}tate and nece{{ls}}{{ls}}itie, be ioyned therevnto. Take heede therfore thou gather not of Chri{{ls}}ts wordes, that Chri{{ls}}tian men {{ls}}hould haue no v{{ls}}e of external office towards God: for that would take away al {{ls}}acrifice, Sacraments, praiers, Churches, and {{ls}}ocietie of men in his Seruice.
